<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914519_theRebbe_363" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914519_theRebbe_363__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section opens the maamar with the heading for Simchat Torah 5740.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">The day of Simchat Torah, 5740.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section raises questions about why Shemini Atzeret is called "the eighth day" and why it is specifically connected to Sukkot rather than to Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"On the eighth day, an assembly (Atzeret) shall be for you."</t>
    <t s="1">And the precise observations of our Nesi'im regarding this are well known.</t>
    <t s="2">For Shemini Atzeret is a festival in its own right regarding the matters of PZR KShB.</t>
    <t s="3">And if so, it should have said "on the twenty-second day of the seventh month," like in the other festivals where the day of the month is stated.</t>
    <t s="4">(And in the seventh month, on the first of the month,</t>
    <t s="5">and on the tenth of the seventh month,</t>
    <t s="6">and on the fifteenth day of the seventh month),</t>
    <t s="7">so why does it say "on the eighth day"?</t>
    <t s="8">And although Shemini Atzeret comes in sequence after the seven days of Sukkot,</t>
    <t s="9">and it is known</t>
    <t s="10">that on Shemini Atzeret the matters of the seven days of Sukkot are restrained and absorbed,</t>
    <t s="11">nevertheless, on Shemini Atzeret the matters of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur are also restrained and absorbed,</t>
    <t s="12">and yet it is not called by a name that indicates its connection</t>
    <t s="13">(and that it comes in sequence)</t>
    <t s="14">to Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="15">so why is it called by the name "eighth"</t>
    <t s="16">(Atzeret)?</t>
    <t s="17">And particularly according to the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov</t>
    <t s="18">that this name by which it is called in the Holy Tongue indicates the content of the thing,</t>
    <t s="19">and even indicates its vitality and existence,</t>
    <t s="20">from which it is understood</t>
    <t s="21">that the essential matter of Shemini Atzeret</t>
    <t s="22">(which is called by the name Shemini Atzeret)</t>
    <t s="23">is that it comes in sequence after the seven days of Sukkot.</t>
    <t s="24">Also, one must understand what is written: "an assembly (Atzeret) shall be for you,"</t>
    <t s="25">and it is brought in the Midrash</t>
    <t s="26">as it is stated,</t>
    <t s="27">"They shall be yours alone, and no strangers with you,"</t>
    <t s="28">that there are two matters in this.</t>
    <t s="29">The matter of "yours alone,"</t>
    <t s="30">Israel and the King alone,</t>
    <t s="31">but nevertheless, from this very thing that it is necessary to negate that there are strangers with you, it is understood that there is room for an assumption that Shemini Atzeret is also for strangers, and therefore it is necessary to negate and say that it is only for you.</t>
    <t s="32">Also, one must understand that Shemini Atzeret also includes Simchat Torah,</t>
    <t s="33">to the extent that in the Land of Israel,</t>
    <t s="34">the land which... the eyes of the L-rd your G-d are always upon it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year,</t>
    <t s="35">Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah are on one day,</t>
    <t s="36">and even in the Diaspora, where they are two days, Simchat Torah is on the second day of Shemini Atzeret,</t>
    <t s="37">and the precise point in this is known, that they established Simchat Torah on Shemini Atzeret,</t>
    <t s="38">for ostensibly, they should have made Simchat Torah on the festival of Shavuot, the time of the giving of our Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions why Simchat Torah was established specifically on Shemini Atzeret for the later tablets, and not on Shavuot for the first tablets, and why not immediately after Yom Kippur.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">B)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, in many places</t>
    <t s="2">it is explained that this that we make Simchat Torah on Shemini Atzeret is because of the later tablets that were given on Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="3">but this very thing</t>
    <t s="4">(that the joy of Simchat Torah is specifically over the later tablets and not over the first tablets)</t>
    <t s="5">requires explanation,</t>
    <t s="6">for the primary revelation and perfection of the Giving of the Torah was specifically in the giving of the first tablets,</t>
    <t s="7">both regarding Israel, who were then at the ultimate level of perfection,</t>
    <t s="8">for at the standing at Mount Sinai their impurity ceased,</t>
    <t s="9">and regarding the world, for there was then a revelation of the actual Ein Sof below, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="10">"And the L-rd descended upon Mount Sinai," and the Targum translates, "and He revealed Himself,"</t>
    <t s="11">and this revelation affected the entire world,</t>
    <t s="12">as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said,</t>
    <t s="13">"No bird chirped, no fowl flew, no ox lowed,"</t>
    <t s="14">to the extent that the voice of the Ten Commandments was heard from all four directions and from above and from below,</t>
    <t s="15">so that the world</t>
    <t s="16">(and all the realms of space within it)</t>
    <t s="17">cried out, "I am"</t>
    <t s="18">"the L-rd your G-d...,"</t>
    <t s="19">"You shall not have...,"</t>
    <t s="20">for all this was specifically with the first tablets,</t>
    <t s="21">so why did they establish Simchat Torah on Shemini Atzeret specifically for the later tablets?</t>
    <t s="22">And what is explained in many places,</t>
    <t s="23">that this that we make Simchat Torah specifically over the later tablets is because regarding the later tablets it is written, "He will tell you the secrets of wisdom, for they are double to that which you have,"</t>
    <t s="24">requires explanation,</t>
    <t s="25">for since the matter of the revelation</t>
    <t s="26">(of the Giving of the Torah)</t>
    <t s="27">in Israel and in the world was specifically with the first tablets, as above,</t>
    <t s="28">ostensibly the joy of Simchat Torah, which is with melodies and dances</t>
    <t s="29">(the matter of revelation)</t>
    <t s="30">should be on the festival of Shavuot, on which the first tablets were given, with revelation and publicity.</t>
    <t s="31">And particularly according to what is explained</t>
    <t s="32">regarding the matter of the dances</t>
    <t s="33">(of Simchat Torah)</t>
    <t s="34">that the matter of the dances is primarily with the feet,</t>
    <t s="35">and in them specifically, in the heel of them,</t>
    <t s="36">the lowest part of the person,</t>
    <t s="37">(except that through this, the head is also elevated and dances).</t>
    <t s="38">From this it is understood that the joy of Simchat Torah is primarily not from the aspect of the Torah's activity in Israel, "I am first,"</t>
    <t s="39">but rather,</t>
    <t s="40">from the aspect of the Torah's activity in the world, which is secondary</t>
    <t s="41">to Israel,</t>
    <t s="42">analogous to the feet which are secondary to the head,</t>
    <t s="43">and in the world itself, in its lower matters</t>
    <t s="44">(the aspect of "eikev").</t>
    <t s="45">According to this, it is even more difficult to understand why they established Simchat Torah specifically for the later tablets,</t>
    <t s="46">for the superiority of "double to that which you have" in the later tablets is in Israel.</t>
    <t s="47">Also, it is not understood,</t>
    <t s="48">that according to this</t>
    <t s="49">(that the joy of Simchat Torah is over the later tablets that were given on Yom Kippur)</t>
    <t s="50">they should have made Simchat Torah on the day after Yom Kippur.</t>
    <t s="51">That they did not establish Simchat Torah on Yom Kippur itself, one could say that this is because there is no joy without eating and drinking,</t>
    <t s="52">but it should have been immediately after Yom Kippur.</t>
    <t s="53">And perhaps one could say even more than this,</t>
    <t s="54">for we find that in that year</t>
    <t s="55">(of the inauguration of the Holy Temple)</t>
    <t s="56">Israel did not observe Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="57">and a Heavenly Voice went out and said to them, "You are all invited to the life of the World to Come,"</t>
    <t s="58">because the joy of the inauguration of the Holy Temple is more sublime than the affliction of Yom Kippur.</t>
    <t s="59">And since the joy of Simchat Torah is a very great joy,</t>
    <t s="60">to the extent that it is even greater than the joy of the Simchat Beit HaShoevah,</t>
    <t s="61">for "one who has not seen the Simchat Beit HaShoevah has never seen joy in his life,"</t>
    <t s="62">if so, it would have been fitting to establish Simchat Torah on Yom Kippur itself.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
